text:
maya: Quick question — can we add a console preview that shows the *effective* SLO threshold after noise-adjustments / notify-sampling and quota routing are applied?

maya: Right now the UI shows the raw SLO number and notify policy independently, but teams keep getting surprised when tenant routing/quota + sampling means they never actually get page traffic.

tom: +1 this. We had a pager where the SLO was 99.9 but notify sampling set to 0.1 and tenant quota routed to a lower tier, so no one saw it for hours. Confusing. :grimacing:

ashwin: We should be careful about the API shape. If console shows an “effective threshold” we need a deterministic function: threshold + quiet-windows + sampling + routing-fallbacks -> effective notify decision. Otherwise customers will litigate.

lina: agree. Proposal: preview in UX that says: 1) raw threshold, 2) adjusted threshold (after quieting policies), 3) effective notify probability (0-100%) and 4) routing tier used. Small mock: 

```
raw_slo: 99.9%
quiet_window: 23:00-07:00 (tenant timezone)
notify_sampling: 10%
routing_priority: tenant->soft->shared
effective_notify: 1% (calc: notify_sampling * routing_fallback_multiplier)
```

lina: We can display a red/amber/green dot based on effective_notify and recent alert volume.

maya: How would we compute routing_fallback_multiplier? It needs to reflect per-tenant reserved capacity and current backpressure.

ashwin: Implementation idea: evaluate an ordered policy chain per request: if tenant has reserved capacity -> multiplier=1; else if dedicated pool available -> 0.5; else shared -> 0.1. Those numbers are tunable and should be surfaced in the API as weights.

samira: From an SRE POV we also need to show historical "notify hit rate" for the tenant so product teams can see how often an SLO breach would have produced a page in the last X days. That will make the preview actionable.

tom: For the internal API, suggest an endpoint: GET /v1/tenants/:id/slo/effective?window=30d which returns the computed effective_notify and a breakdown. It should be idempotent and cacheable.

maya: +1. Also need to decide whether the console generates the preview client-side (fetch raw and run sim) or server-side (call service that runs policy logic). Server-side seems better for parity across hosted/dedicated/private.

lina: Server-side for parity. And we can include an optional query param ?simulate_overrides=true to let UI toggle sampling/quieting to preview changes.

ops-bot: deploy-bot: Canary job queued for slo-preview-service v1.3 -> env=staging (job 58921)

maya: Nice. A couple of UX edgecases: 1) avoid leaking capacity signals across tenants in preview (show only coarse tiers), 2) make clear that effective_notify is a projection, not a guarantee.

ashwin: Also need a contract for privacy: the preview cannot return exact tenant IDs of routes used for fallback. Just tier names and aggregated rates.

samira: On alerts side, we should expose a checkbox: "Show console-opt-in estimate of pages per week" so on-call teams can estimate bandwidth. That box defaults off.

tom: Implementation checklist from my side: API + caching layer, small sampling simulator library (we already have one in eng-sre), telemetry metrics (preview_requests_total, preview_cached_hit, preview_simulated_pages_estimate).

maya: Can someone own a short RFC? 1 pager with API path, example response, privacy constraints, and UI mock. I can draft initial doc.

lina: I can add the UI mock and copy text for the tooltip.

ashwin: I'll draft API contract and the fallback-weight table.

samira: I'll list the telemetry and a proposal for the histogram we want for "simulated pages/week" so we can set sensible defaults.

maya: Thanks — will ping when RFC draft is up. :rocket:
